learning: Iterations 0 to 5 show that pitch, footprint, track, gains and mass leave max_error at the 0.06 m floor and one line loss per run. If progress rises but line losses persist, the next test is the lag lever (sensor bar at y = 0.06 m). If progress does not rise, the speed hypothesis is weakened and the sensor bar move is the next step.
notes: Wheel-radius-only test from the iteration 5 design (0.030 to 0.035 m). Controller is unchanged so the result isolates top speed. Measurements include controller_errors and control_effort to catch integration faults.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 5 ended off_track in all 360 trials. max_error stayed at the 0.060 to 0.068 m off-track floor, line_loss_events stayed at 1 per run after the footprint change, and steering_oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.16), so the robot drifts rather than jitters. Pitch (10 to 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), track (0.12 to 0.10 m), kp (1.2 to 1.4) and mass (0.8 to 0.4 kg) each left max_error and line losses essentially unchanged. Progress has stayed at 0.10 to 0.18, so top speed is the untested lever. The Builder's entity0 changes only wheel_radius, from 0.030 to 0.035 m. I build exactly that geometry on the iteration 5 controller, with the controller held fixed so any change in progress or line losses is attributable to wheel radius. Gains are unchanged (kp 1.4, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). The sensor bar stays at y = 0.04 m, because lag has not yet been tested alone and the Builder's rule defers it until line losses clear. Turn per unit PWM depends on wheel_track, which is unchanged, so steering authority should stay about the same while ground speed rises about 17 percent. Measurements include controller_errors and control_effort to catch integration faults.
